page: Vultr vcg-a16-6c-60g-16vram is an x86_64 server configuration classified under the Dedicated Metal GPU family, though provisioned with zero active GPUs. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, configured with 3 physical cores and 6 vCPUs via multithreading. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory provisioning is substantial, supplying 60.0 GB of RAM, which equates to an elevated ratio of 10.0 GB per vCPU. Local persistence is provided by an integrated 350 GB NVMe solid-state drive.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate mid-tier computing and memory bandwidth throughput. The instance recorded a single-core Geekbench score of 1423.0 and a multi-core score of 6248.0, aligning with an overall PassMark CPU score of 10812.15 and stress-ng multi-core metric of 10002.52. High-bandwidth cached memory read operations reach 590.4 GB/sec, while uncached reads and writes perform at 60.86 GB/sec and 34.59 GB/sec. Conversely, the server registered weak results in the PassMark memory evaluation (1766.17) and database operations benchmark (2554.74), alongside multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 30.4 GB/sec.

With a high memory-to-vCPU allocation, the instance delivers a practical resource profile for memory-sensitive tasks that do not demand extreme core parallelization. The 350 GB NVMe drive supports localized data access, and network performance is supported with one complimentary public IPv4 address. Its CPU-based machine learning inference is restricted, registering under 5 tokens per second on 7B LLM models, indicating it is better aligned with in-memory caching, mid-sized data extraction, software compilation, and medium-scale web application serving.
description: Vultr vcg-a16-6c-60g-16vram is a dedicated x86_64 instance featuring an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.0 GHz with 3 physical cores and 6 vCPUs. It integrates 60.0 GB of system memory, providing an extensive 10.0 GB per thread, combined with 350 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD local storage. In benchmark assessments, the system delivers solid mid-range performance with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6248.0, a PassMark CPU score of 10812.15, and uncached sequential memory read bandwidth of 60.86 GB/sec. However, lower scores in PassMark database operations and multi-threaded decompression highlight hardware limits during concurrent intensive throughput. The absence of an active GPU further limits compute capability for deep learning workflows. This configuration functions efficiently for memory-demanding services, distributed in-memory caching nodes, staging platforms, and general web workloads that require ample RAM per core.
